newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank holds interest rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank holds interest rates steady.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.
The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at three percent.

A Reuter poll of economists this week showed that none of the 10 polled expected any change in the central bank's credit policies this week and German bond and share markets showed almost no response to the expected move.
There had been some talk in financial markets on Wednesday of a further ease in the securities repurchase rate, but most traders had dismissed the rumour, saying such a move was unlikely.

In fact, most economists have now come to the conclusion that German rates may finally have bottomed at current levels, with all of those polled this week predicting no further rate cuts in this interest rate cycle.
The discount and repo rates are already at historic lows.
